target.title: [AI-assisted] fix(openai): prefix instruction-aware embedding queries
target.body:
## Summary

AI-assisted PR.

- Problem: OpenAI-compatible embedding providers pass raw query text to instruction-aware embedding models such as Qwen3 and Mixedbread unless the operator handles query formatting outside OpenClaw.
- Why it matters: Raw retrieval queries can produce lower-quality embeddings for models whose contracts expect query-side prompting.
- What changed: OpenAI and generic `openai-compatible` memory embeddings now support opt-in `memorySearch.queryInstructionTemplate: true`, applying shared Qwen3/Mixedbread query templates only to query embeddings.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Defaults remain raw; document/batch embeddings remain raw; credentials, base URL behavior, and non-OpenAI providers are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** With `memorySearch.queryInstructionTemplate: true`, bundled OpenAI and generic `openai-compatible` embedding providers apply the shared Qwen3 query instruction template to query embeddings only. With the option disabled or omitted, query text remains raw. Document/batch embeddings remain raw in both modes.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw development checkout at exact PR head `4d6adf6cdd28de1c23eb89b35111236b0fa5f622`, using configured model `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-4B`. A local OpenAI-compatible loopback `/v1/embeddings` endpoint captured emitted request bodies and returned 2560-dimensional fixture vectors; credentials and the loopback port were redacted.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran `corepack pnpm exec tsx tmp/pr-79702-exact-head-proof.mts` from the PR worktree after the 2026-07-17 rebase. The script exercised both provider paths in enabled and disabled modes: bundled OpenAI query/document embeddings and generic `openai-compatible` query/document embeddings.

**Observed result after fix:** Both provider paths returned 2560-dimensional vectors in enabled and disabled modes. Enabled query request bodies were prefixed with `Instruct: Given a user query, retrieve relevant memory notes and documents\nQuery:...`; disabled query request bodies stayed raw; document request bodies stayed raw in both modes.

**What was not tested:** Every OpenAI-compatible embedding server and model family was not tested. This proof covers the shared Qwen3 template behavior and the enabled/disabled contract for both affected provider paths.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: The OpenAI-compatible embedding paths did not have a shared, opt-in way to mirror the instruction-aware query-prefix handling already used by other memory embedding providers.
- Missing detection / guardrail: Unit tests did not verify provider-specific query payloads for instruction-aware models.
- Contributing context (if known): Some OpenAI-compatible servers expose embedding models that expect different query and document input formatting even when they use an OpenAI-style `/embeddings` API.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
 - [x] Unit test
 - [ ] Seam / integration test
 - [ ] End-to-end test
 - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target tests/files: `extensions/openai/embedding-provider.test.ts`, `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts`, `src/agents/memory-search.test.ts`, and `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts`.
- Scenario the tests should lock in: The opt-in flag propagates through memory-search provider creation; Qwen3/Mixedbread query embeddings include the expected query instruction prefix only when enabled; document batch embeddings and disabled/default queries remain raw.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The behavior is local to provider request payload construction plus memory-search config propagation.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): N/A
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

OpenAI-compatible memory embedding providers can now opt into query instruction templates for known instruction-aware embedding models via `memorySearch.queryInstructionTemplate: true`. Defaults remain raw, and document embeddings are unchanged.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Default:
[memory search query] -> [raw query embedding input]

Opt-in:
[memory search query] -> [model-specific query instruction prefix] -> [embedding input]

Documents:
[indexed memory/document] -> [raw document embedding input]
```

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux
- Runtime/container: Local OpenClaw development checkout
- Model/provider: `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-4B` through an OpenAI-compatible loopback endpoint for exact request capture
- Integration/channel (if any): OpenClaw memorySearch provider construction and embedding provider adapters
- Relevant config (redacted): `memorySearch.queryInstructionTemplate: true` for enabled proof cases; omitted/false for disabled proof cases; endpoint port and API key redacted.

### Steps

1. Configure bundled OpenAI and generic `openai-compatible` memory embedding providers with `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-4B`.
2. Exercise query and document embedding calls with `queryInstructionTemplate: true`.
3. Exercise query and document embedding calls with `queryInstructionTemplate` disabled.
4. Compare captured `/v1/embeddings` request bodies.

### Expected

- Enabled query embeddings for Qwen3 include the shared query instruction prefix.
- Disabled/default query embeddings remain raw.
- Document embeddings are not query-prefixed.

### Actual

- Enabled query embeddings for both provider paths were prefixed as expected.
- Disabled query embeddings for both provider paths stayed raw.
- Document embedding payloads stayed raw in both modes.

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: Exact-head enabled and disabled request-capture proof for bundled OpenAI and generic `openai-compatible`; focused unit tests for prefixed query embeddings and raw document embeddings.
- Edge cases checked: Disabled/default queries stay raw; document calls stay raw; the public Plugin SDK API baseline and surface budget match the new helper/option.
- What you did **not** verify: Every OpenAI-compatible embedding server or additional instruction-aware model family beyond the covered Qwen3/Mixedbread templates.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`) Yes, optional `memorySearch.queryInstructionTemplate: true`
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: A provider could expose a matching model ID but expect raw query input.
 - Mitigation: The behavior is opt-in and default-false; document embeddings remain unchanged.
- Risk: The config/plugin SDK surface becomes a long-lived compatibility contract.
 - Mitigation: The helper centralizes the policy and keeps provider behavior consistent, but maintainer approval is still needed for the public contract.
